images.alt_grc: χειμὼν ἦν· οἱ παῖδες μετὰ τοῦ πάππου παρὰ τῷ πυρὶ ἦσαν.
images.alt_en: An old man seated, telling a story; children listen (terracotta group or vase scene).

images.alt_grc: ἡ Ῥέα τῷ Κρόνῳ λίθον ἐν σπαργάνοις δίδωσιν.
images.alt_en: Rhea hands Kronos the stone wrapped in swaddling clothes (Attic red-figure pelike by the Nausicaa Painter, c. 460 BC, Metropolitan Museum 06.1021.144).

images.alt_grc: οἱ Κούρητες τοῖς δόρασι τὰς ἀσπίδας κρούουσιν περὶ τὸν παῖδα.
images.alt_en: The armed Kouretes clash spears on shields around the infant Zeus (Roman terracotta Campana relief).

images.alt_grc: τὸ ἄντρον
images.alt_en: The Dictaean cave on Crete, the traditional birthplace of Zeus: a cave mouth in the rock.

images.alt_grc: ἡ ἀσπίς
images.alt_en: A round hoplite shield (bronze shield facing or a vase painting of a warrior's shield).

images.alt_grc: τὸ δόρυ
images.alt_en: A hoplite with his spear raised, from a red-figure vase.

images.alt_grc: ὁ ὀμφαλὸς ὁ ἐν Δελφοῖς.
images.alt_en: The marble omphalos, the 'navel of the world', carved with a net of wool fillets (Delphi Archaeological Museum).

images.alt_grc: ἡ ἱερὰ ἐλαία ἐν τῇ ἀκροπόλει.
images.alt_en: The olive tree beside the Erechtheion on the Acropolis, planted where the sacred olive grew.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κέκροψ· τὸ μὲν ἄνω ἀνδρός, τὸ δὲ κάτω δράκοντος.
images.alt_en: Kekrops, a king whose body ends in a serpent's coils, on an Attic red-figure vase.

images.alt_grc: ἡ Ἀθηνᾶ καὶ ὁ Ποσειδῶν ἐρίζουσιν· ἐν μέσῳ ἡ ἐλαία.
images.alt_en: Athena and Poseidon contend for Attica with the olive tree between them (red-figure hydria from Pella, 4th century BC, after the Parthenon's west pediment).

images.alt_grc: ἡ τρίαινα
images.alt_en: Poseidon holding his trident, from a black- or red-figure vase.

images.alt_grc: ὁ δράκων
images.alt_en: A great serpent coiled around a tree or rising up, from a Greek vase painting.

images.alt_grc: τὸ ἀέτωμα τὸ πρὸς ἑσπέραν τοῦ Παρθενῶνος.
images.alt_en: Drawing of 1674 (attributed to Jacques Carrey) of the west pediment of the Parthenon: Athena and Poseidon spring apart in the centre.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἀκρίσιος τὴν Δανάην ἐν θαλάμῳ χαλκῷ φρουρεῖ.
images.alt_en: Danae in her bronze chamber (Attic red-figure vase).

images.alt_grc: ἡ Δανάη καὶ ὁ Περσεὺς εἰς τὴν λάρνακα εἰσβαίνουσιν.
images.alt_en: Akrisios watches as Danae, holding the baby Perseus, is put into the wooden chest (Attic red-figure hydria, c. 490 BC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Περσεὺς τὴν τῆς Μεδούσης κεφαλὴν ἔχων φεύγει.
images.alt_en: Perseus runs off with the head of Medusa in his bag; the body of the Gorgon sinks behind him (Attic red-figure hydria by the Pan Painter, c. 460 BC, Metropolitan Museum 45.11.1).

images.alt_grc: ἡ λάρναξ
images.alt_en: A wooden chest with a lid, as painted on vases of Danae and Perseus.

images.alt_grc: τὰ πτερωτὰ πέδιλα
images.alt_en: Winged sandals, as worn by Hermes and Perseus on vase paintings.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Αἰγεὺς τὴν Θέμιν ἐν Δελφοῖς ἐρωτᾷ.
images.alt_en: King Aegeus consults the Delphic oracle; the priestess sits on the tripod (Attic red-figure kylix by the Codrus Painter, c. 440 BC, Berlin F 2538).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ζεὺς ὅμοιος Ἀμφιτρύωνι γενόμενος πρὸς τὴν Ἀλκμήνην ἔρχεται.
images.alt_en: Zeus comes to Alcmene at night (South Italian or Attic vase with Zeus, Alcmene or Amphitryon).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἡρακλῆς βρέφος ὢν τοὺς δράκοντας ἄγχει.
images.alt_en: The infant Heracles strangles the two serpents while Iphicles cries out (Attic red-figure stamnos by the Berlin Painter, c. 480 BC, Louvre G 192).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἡρακλῆς παῖς ὢν μετὰ τῆς τροφοῦ εἰς τὸ διδασκαλεῖον βαδίζει.
images.alt_en: Young Heracles walks to his music lesson behind his old nurse Geropso, who carries his lyre (Attic red-figure skyphos by the Pistoxenos Painter, c. 470 BC, Schwerin).

images.alt_grc: ἡ εὐνή
images.alt_en: A child's cradle or a couch with a sleeping figure, from a Greek vase or terracotta.

images.alt_grc: ἡ κιθάρα
images.alt_en: A musician playing the kithara, the large concert lyre (Attic red-figure amphora, Berlin Painter, Metropolitan Museum 56.171.38).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἡρακλῆς τὸν Λίνον τύπτει.
images.alt_en: Heracles attacks his music teacher Linus with a stool (Attic red-figure kylix by Douris, c. 480 BC, Munich).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Εὐρυσθεὺς τῷ Ἡρακλεῖ τοὺς ἄθλους ἐπιτάττει.
images.alt_en: Heracles, with lion skin and club, before King Eurystheus (Attic black-figure vase).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἡρακλῆς τὸν λέοντα ἄγχει.
images.alt_en: Heracles wrestles the Nemean lion, his arm locked round its neck (Attic black-figure amphora, 6th century BC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Εὐρυσθεὺς ἐν τῷ πίθῳ κρύπτεται.
images.alt_en: King Eurystheus hides in a great storage jar sunk in the ground while Heracles brings him a monster (Attic black-figure vase).

images.alt_grc: ὁ λέων
images.alt_en: A lion, from a Greek sculpture or vase (e.g. a marble funerary lion).

images.alt_grc: τὸ ῥόπαλον
images.alt_en: Heracles' club, as held by a bronze statuette of the hero.

images.alt_grc: ὁ πίθος
images.alt_en: A large clay storage jar (pithos).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἡρακλῆς νέος ὑπὲρ τοῦ λέοντος ἕστηκεν.
images.alt_en: Metope from the temple of Zeus at Olympia, c. 460 BC: the young Heracles stands exhausted over the dead Nemean lion, with Athena and Hermes (Archaeological Museum of Olympia).

images.alt_grc: ἡ ναῦς μέλαν ἱστίον ἔχουσα εἰς Κρήτην πλεῖ.
images.alt_en: A Greek ship under sail (Attic black-figure cup or dinos with a ship).

images.alt_grc: ἡ Ἀριάδνη τῷ Θησεῖ τὸ λίνον δίδωσιν.
images.alt_en: Ariadne hands Theseus the ball of thread before he enters the Labyrinth (Greek vase painting).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Θησεὺς τὸν Μινώταυρον ἀποκτείνει.
images.alt_en: Theseus kills the bull-headed Minotaur (Attic black-figure amphora, 6th century BC).

images.alt_grc: τὸ ἱστίον
images.alt_en: A ship's square sail on its mast, from a Greek vase.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Θησεὺς τὸν Μινώταυρον ἐκ τοῦ λαβυρίνθου ἕλκει.
images.alt_en: Theseus drags the dead Minotaur out of the Labyrinth while Athena watches (Attic red-figure kylix by Aison, c. 420 BC, National Archaeological Museum, Madrid).
